prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
for the development of base editing, programmable chemical editing of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is the cleanest chemistry case on the list. Aryl amines from aryl halides went from a harsh, substrate-limited problem to a routine disconnection through mechanism-guided ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines, chelating bisphosphines). Its adoption is visible in countless total syntheses, in medicinal chemistry and in process routes to marketed drugs. Attribution is unusually tidy: two independent groups developed the general catalytic systems, with Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide precedent a clear precursor but not the general method. As a second part I support base editing for David Liu alone. It is a chemically conceived idea, directing deaminase chemistry to a chosen base inside the genome, and it is already in the clinic. Liu is the clear intellectual driver of both editor classes, which keeps the union at three people and avoids a sprawling credit list. Pairing a core molecule-making method with a chemical-biology tool gives a prize that spans the field.
statement.case_against: C-N coupling is a refinement of a coupling paradigm that was recognised in 2010 (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki), so some will say the conceptual step is smaller, and its leaders may seem more incremental than a new modality. Base editing is protein engineering and genome biology at least as much as chemistry; genome-editing chemistry was already recognised with CRISPR-Cas9 in 2020, and the Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo credit needs careful handling. Pairing the two parts means each person gets only half a prize's worth of attention, and the pairing has no unifying theme beyond 'catalysis meets selectivity'.

responses.point: Heiner ranks Pd C-N coupling first as a clear, general mechanistic principle with a new capability, and ranks nanopore sequencing second and base editing fourth, proposing Hartwig and Buchwald with Liu as a separate option.
responses.response: I agree on B039 and on Buchwald and Hartwig as the decisive pair. I would not widen the credit to Kosugi, because the later general catalytic systems, not the stoichiometric tin chemistry, made the reaction routine. On base editing I think Heiner's cautious fourth place understates it, since the chemistry of the deaminase fusion is new and general. I do share his wish for a clean mechanistic story, which is why I limit credit to Liu.

responses.point: Johan ranks base editing first as a game-changer, a chemically conceived deaminase fusion with a new capability and clinical uptake, with Liu as the sole laureate, and puts PROTACs second.
responses.response: We agree that Liu alone is the defensible attribution. Komor and Gaudelli were essential trainees, but Liu conceived and directed both editors, and a three-person cap leaves no room for trainees. Where I qualify his case is that base editing alone does not make a chemistry prize for me. It is strongest as one part of a two-achievement prize, and I would not make it the sole headline and leave out a core synthetic method.

responses.point: Andrei ranks base editing first and proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, arguing the two first-author discoverers should share credit alongside Liu.
responses.response: I disagree on attribution, though the argument is serious. Naming Komor and Gaudelli would push the union to four with Buchwald and Hartwig, and it would break the 'two distinct achievements' configuration at the three-person limit. Nobel precedent for PI-led tool development favours the group leader. I would reconsider only if the committee drops the second part.

responses.point: Emma ranks biomolecular phase separation first and lipid nanoparticles second, as physical-chemical principles with huge reach, and puts Pd C-N coupling sixth.
responses.response: I see the conceptual breadth of condensates, but I ask what was new chemically, and I have trouble locating a single mechanism or decisive experiment that defines the achievement. The attribution among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is also loose. C-N coupling can be pointed to in the literature, and its use is measured in thousands of syntheses. I will take the condensate case seriously if a clearer chemical formulation can be given.

responses.point: Xiaodong ranks zeolite and molecular-sieve design first on the strength of industrial catalysis and separations, with Corma, Davis and Zones proposed.
responses.response: I accept that molecular sieves have a huge industrial footprint and are genuinely chemistry, so I keep B033 as an alternative. My reservations are about a single decisive discovery, because the credit spreads across many framework syntheses and the field is broad, and about attribution across Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis. Pd amination has a sharper, more verifiable origin and an equally broad downstream footprint.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will see C-N coupling as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether base editing is judged mainly as chemistry or as genome engineering, and whether Komor and Gaudelli should share credit.
Whether the two-part pairing is acceptable or the committee prefers a single thematic prize.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are mature enough, given pending approval of a bifunctional degrader.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I share Lund University with Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, which is an ordinary colleague connection and not a recusal issue, and I have no known tie to any shortlisted candidate.
